transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (CTO, SilverLake), Priya Rao (Head of Platform), Luis Martinez (SRE), Aisha Khan (PM)

00:00 Olivia Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um I'm Olivia I'll run a quick agenda, Marcus will demo the Console and the API snippets for rate limiting and org/project keys
00:12 Jared Kim: Awesome thanks Olivia, Jared here, we grabbed some time because we're trying to nail down multi-tenant controls for the new patient-facing assistant, want to understand quotas and per-customer constraints
00:23 Marcus Patel: cool, so quick context, we'll show the Console policies, the API key model - org keys + project keys, then a couple of rate limit policies and how they map to projects. There may be a little lag while I pull up the dashboard, sorry if audio is fuzzy
00:38 Priya Rao: no problem, quick qual Q - currently we run a mix of in-house microservices on EKS and some workloads on AWS lambda, we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated endpoints, security is a blocker for us
00:52 Marcus Patel: understood, we'll surface the VPC/private control plane options and the Dedicated path as well. For security we'll highlight audit logs, KMS integration, SAML SSO and RBAC in the console
01:06 Luis Martinez: For SRE concerns, we need per-tenant rate limiting and the ability to throttle a single misbehaving tenant without impacting others, is that supported?
01:15 Marcus Patel: yes, that's where project keys come in. Org key authenticates the whole account, project keys are issued per-app or per-tenant. You can attach rate limit policies at the project-level or org-level, and set hard quotas + soft burst allowances
01:30 Olivia Chen: i'll also add that our routing supports fallback to cheaper model variants if quota is exceeded or Dedicated capacity is constrained, so the app stays up albeit at a different latency/cost point
01:43 Jared Kim: curious about enforcement surface - is it token-based, request-based, or both? e.g., if a tenant sends long contexts will that eat into quota differently?
01:53 Marcus Patel: good Q - you can configure both. Our policy engine supports per-token budgets and per-request concurrency caps. Example: 100k tokens/month per project + 10 rps spike limit. The Console visualizes projected spend based on token estimates
02:09 Priya Rao: that token estimate calc - is it client side or do you serve estimates in responses? We need to show estimated billing to product teams
02:18 Marcus Patel: the Console uses recent usage patterns to estimate token burn and projected monthly spend, and the API returns token counts in the response metadata so you can display it client-side
02:30 Aisha Khan: can we set hard cutoffs per tenant and send custom webhook when cutoff happens?
02:36 Marcus Patel: yes, you can define policy actions: block, queue, or route to a fallback model. And you can hook webhooks or internal alerts for policy events. We also have metrics shipped to your monitoring endpoints
02:49 Jared Kim: show us the console please
03:02 Marcus Patel: switching over... ok here's the org-level page. Top right shows org keys, below are projects. This example org has three projects: web-chat, mobile, and research. If i click web-chat you see project key, quota config, and role bindings
03:20 Marcus Patel: i can create a new project and issue a project-specific key, note the key scope is limited to only that project's routes, you can't use it to access other projects unless you explicitly grant it
03:31 Luis Martinez: nice, so that means if we leak a project key the blast radius is limited, correct?
03:35 Marcus Patel: correct, blast radius is limited. Also keys can be rotated via the Console or API and you can set expiry
03:44 Priya Rao: what about rate limit enforcement latency? we don't want synchronous blocking adding latency to user requests
03:51 Marcus Patel: enforcement runs in the control plane asynchronously with low-latency checks in the serving plane; typical additional latency is sub-ms for local checks, but depends on your model path. We can show latency numbers from our benchmarks
04:05 Olivia Chen: to add, for Dedicated customers we can run an enforcement proxy inside your VPC which keeps checks local to avoid cross-region calls
04:15 Jared Kim: security review question - audit logs, retention, and how logs show policy hits per project?
04:23 Marcus Patel: audit logs are shipped to your S3 or GCS, we also integrate with SIEMs. Logs include request metadata, key used, project id, policy decision, and token counts. Retention configurable via plan or add-on
04:38 Aisha Khan: do you support customer-managed keys?
04:42 Marcus Patel: yes KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and Dedicated customers. Hosted customers get envelope encryption and we can enable customer-managed KMS in many regions
04:52 Jared Kim: can you show an API example for issuing project keys and applying a quota?
04:56 Marcus Patel: sure, open the API docs tab... here's a curl: curl -X POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects -d '{"name":"pilot-tenant-42"}' then curl to create key and attach policy: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/policies -d '{"type":"quota","tokens_per_month":2000000,"action":"block","webhook_url":"https://ops.silverlake/rl"}'
05:28 Priya Rao: small transcription note, the JSON in the Console GUI is prettified, but sometimes placeholders are odd in the auto copy, just small thing
05:38 Luis Martinez: what's the difference between quota "block" and quota "queue"?
05:42 Marcus Patel: block immediately rejects new requests once quota exceeded; queue puts them in a short FIFO buffer up to configured time window; queue useful for smoothing spikes without failing user requests
05:55 Jared Kim: for compliance we need proof that per-tenant data isn't intermingled - are logs and telemetry partitioned by project id?
06:03 Marcus Patel: yes, telemetry and KV cache keys are namespaced per-project; you can also run separate Dedicated pools per-tenant for strict isolation (higher cost)
06:18 Aisha Khan: do you have an example pricing for a pilot like ours? we expect around 1.2M tokens/month across 10 tenants, peak 20 qps
06:26 Olivia Chen: we usually propose a short pilot on Hosted with org/project keys and a capped spend for the month. Pricing we'll send in the follow-up but ballpark we can support that under our standard tier or a small reserved commit if you want predictability
06:40 Jared Kim: what about fallback model quality? we can't drop to a very low-quality model in front of patients
06:47 Marcus Patel: fallback path is configurable, you can pick comparable open models or fall back to a cached response. Also Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles that reduce cost without big quality regressions
06:59 Priya Rao: will optimize recommendations be applied automatically? or are they suggestions we have to opt into?
07:06 Marcus Patel: suggestions only; we don't change model configs without explicit approval. Optimize provides recommended quantization and batching settings and estimated impact on latency/cost per route
07:18 Jared Kim: any customers in healthcare using Dedicated? we want references for compliance checks
07:22 Olivia Chen: yes a few health systems use Dedicated + Private control plane, we'll include reference contacts in the security pack link. had one note where they needed annual pen test evidence - we shared our SOC2 report and architecture diagrams
07:36 Luis Martinez: on outage behavior - if your hosted region has capacity issues can we route to another region or Dedicated fallback?
07:44 Marcus Patel: yes Smart Routing policies let you route by region, latency or cost and you can set automatic fallback to another region or a cheaper model variant or your Dedicated pool
07:58 Aisha Khan: can we create enforcement that reduces per-tenant concurrency before cutting tokens? like degrade assistant features first
08:06 Marcus Patel: absolutely, policy actions are pluggable. Example: first degrade to summary-only responses, then reduce max tokens per response, then block. The Console lets you set policy chains visually
08:22 Jared Kim: show the audit log sample
08:25 Marcus Patel: opening logs... here's a sample event: {timestamp, org_id, project_id, key_id, policy_decision:\"block\", tokens:512, route:\"gpt-open-1\", request_id:\"...\"} - note in transcripts sometimes names get munged but fields are stable
08:41 Priya Rao: ok this looks fit for purpose. couple questions on quota enforcement windows - sliding window vs calendar month?
08:50 Marcus Patel: supports both sliding and calendar based windows; sliding gives smoother behavior if you want, calendar easier for billing alignment
09:00 Jared Kim: for pilot we want: org keys + project keys per tenant, per-tenant 200k tokens/month, webhook on cutoff, dashboard access for product, and a scheduled benchmark run with latency targets - can you do that?
09:12 Olivia Chen: yep that's doable. we'll scope the pilot in the follow-up. Marcus can run a benchmark on our sample workload and we'll supply expected test harness steps
09:20 Marcus Patel: I'll need API keys for a test org or we can spin a sandbox. prefer you provide sample payloads and traffic shape so our benchmark matches reality
09:28 Jared Kim: can do, we'll provide payload shapes and peak concurrency details by 3/18
09:34 Olivia Chen: great, recap next steps: Olivia send pricing + security pack, Marcus send benchmark spreadsheet + example configs, SilverLake to send payloads and token estimates; schedule kickoff week of 3/23
09:48 Priya Rao: thanks, appreciate the thoroughness, slight audio hiccup earlier but this was very helpful
09:55 Olivia Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links, going to drop the security pack and the example curl commands. bye
10:00 Meeting end

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription errors e.g. \"gpt-open-1\" vs \"gpt opan one\", generic speaker labels appear for a brief moment. References shared: security pack (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), sample policy JSON in Console
